The Wake

Every boat on deep water opens the same wedge — 19.47°, whatever it is and however fast it goes. Drag to walk around it. Swing the brass arm to measure. Then take the water away from under it.

checking…
drawing the water…
the wedge
the wedge, exactly— measured off the water— brightest water at— the arm reads— wavelength astern— depth Froude, U/√gh—

the boat, and the water under it
the edge, at five radii

No wave height is claimed anywhere in this room. The drawn steepness is linear theory for a Gaussian pressure patch, normalised for exposure and soft-clipped so the far arms stay visible. Every angle comes from the phase alone — from c(k) = U cos θ and from the exact c² = (g/k) tanh kh, and from nothing else.
